mainTopic: Caring for and using a found item (אבידה), and when one may leave a lost item alone
overview: The גמרא first finishes a line from the previous page about workers with oxen, who can cause big losses. It then asks about the משנה's rule on airing out a found garment: what if spreading it helps both the garment and the finder's honor? Proofs from the משנה, from a ברייתא about guests, and from the calf of עגלה ערופה are each pushed aside. Along the way, רב פפא shows from how the word עֻבַּד is written and read that work disqualifies the animal only when the owner is pleased with it. Next, a ברייתא explains how a finder may use found vessels without damaging them, and says gold and glass may not be touched at all. The same rules apply to a פקדון whose owner went overseas. Finally, the גמרא learns from the word וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ that there are times one may leave a lost item, and starts asking which case that פסוק is really needed for. The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Workers with oxen cause big losses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the earlier statement that hiring workers and not supervising them wastes money. This refers to workers using oxen, which can do a lot of damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is talking about oxen, whose damage is great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing out the discussion from the previous page. It explains which unsupervised workers cause a big loss: workers with oxen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary unsupervised workers might only waste a little time. Workers with oxen can let the animals trample and ruin crops, so leaving them alone really does destroy a person's money. This line ties off that topic before the גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה.

phrases.english: With oxen, whose damage is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the previous page's discussion of how a person can waste his inheritance.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of unsupervised workers means workers with oxen, where the possible damage is large.

steps.title: What if spreading it helps both him and the garment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a finder may spread a found garment for its own good, but not for his own honor. It then asks about a case where both reasons apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: he spreads it out for its sake, but not for his own honor. A question was asked: if it is both for his sake and for its sake, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and raises a question about it. This sets up the attempted proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covers two clear cases. Spreading the garment purely to air it out is allowed. Spreading it purely to show off is forbidden. The question is about the mixed case, where it airs out the garment and also makes the finder look good.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked to them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: He spreads it out for its sake
but not for his own honor, etc.
A question was asked to them:
For his sake and for its sake, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a finder may spread out a found garment when it serves both the garment's needs and his own honor.

steps.title: Proof from the first half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the wording "for its sake" that only spreading purely for the garment is allowed, so the mixed case is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "He spreads it out for its sake." For its sake, yes. That implies for his sake and its sake together, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question using the first half of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only permits spreading "for its sake." Reading it closely, that seems to mean only when it is purely for the garment. Once the finder's own benefit is mixed in, it would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a proof is about to be brought)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"He spreads it out for its sake."
For its sake, yes.
But for his sake and for its sake, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the mixed case (both his sake and its sake) is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A close reading of the משנה's first half: "שׁוֹטְחָהּ לְצוֹרְכָּהּ".

steps.title: The second half points the other way, so no proof
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the משנה only forbids spreading purely for his honor, which implies the mixed case is allowed. Since the two halves clash, the משנה cannot settle the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the end of the משנה: "but not for his own honor." Only for his honor is it forbidden. That implies for its sake and his sake together, it is fine. So nothing can be learned from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the second half of the משנה closely too. It concludes that the משנה gives no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half implies the mixed case is forbidden. The second half implies it is allowed. When the two halves of a משנה point in opposite directions, neither close reading can be trusted, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: say the end part (of the source)
nothing can be learned from it

steps.whatToRemember: When the beginning and end of a משנה lead to opposite conclusions about a middle case, the גמרא says the משנה can't decide it.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the mixed case is allowed. It is only saying this משנה can't prove it either way.

phrases.english: Say the end of the משנה:
"but not for his own honor."
It is only for his honor that he may not,
but for its sake and his sake, it is perfectly fine.
Rather, nothing can be learned from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the משנה as proof in either direction.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The close reading of the first half is cancelled out by an opposite close reading of the second half.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא about guests
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when guests come, the finder may not spread the garment at all, even for its sake. This seems to show the mixed case is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: He may not spread it on a bed or on a hanger for his own sake, but he may spread it on a bed or a hanger for its sake. If guests happened to come, he may not spread it on a bed or on a hanger, whether for his sake or for its sake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, to try again to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally spreading for the garment's sake is allowed. But when guests are present, spreading it also shows off to them, so it becomes a mixed case. The ברייתא forbids it even "for its sake," which seems to prove the mixed case is forbidden.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשְׁטָחֶנָּה לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה
phrases.english: He may not spread it, not on a bed
and not on a hanger, for his own sake,
but he may spread it on a bed
and on a hanger for its sake.
If guests happened to come to him,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשְׁטָחֶנָּה לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה
phrases.english: he may not spread it, not on a bed
and not on a hanger,
whether for his sake or for its sake!
phrases.notes: With guests there, even spreading it for the garment also shows off to them. That is why this looks like the mixed case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא יִשְׁטָחֶנָּה לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה failed to decide the question, the גמרא tries a ברייתא instead.
steps.raayaObject: That spreading the garment for both his sake and its sake is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding spreading the garment when guests are present, even for its sake.

steps.title: Spreading before guests actually harms the garment
steps.stepSummary: The guest case proves nothing about the mixed case, because spreading the garment in front of guests puts it at risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. Spreading it in front of guests is like burning it up, either because of the evil eye or because of thieves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the guest ברייתא in Step 5. Spreading the garment in front of guests is not really good for the garment, so that case tells us nothing about a true mixed case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed the guest case was 'for its sake and for his sake' and was still forbidden. The גמרא answers that with guests around, spreading it puts the garment in danger: it can draw an evil eye, or tempt thieves who now know it is there. So the ban comes from that danger, and our mixed question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; a standard way to push aside a proof
He is 'burning it up', meaning he is ruining it
The (evil) eye, harm caused by jealous looks

phrases.english: It is different there,
because he is burning it up
phrases.notes: Not real fire. Showing it off to guests is just as bad for the garment as destroying it.

phrases.english: either because of the evil eye,
or because of thieves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the guest ברייתא; the question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The guest case is not a real mixed case, because spreading before guests endangers the garment (evil eye, thieves).

steps.title: A new proof from the calf placed in a yoke
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about the calf of עגלה ערופה says that putting it in a yoke both to nurse and to thresh makes it unfit. That looks like a mixed case that is treated as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he brought it into the team of cows and it threshed, it is fit. If he did it so that it would nurse and thresh, it is unfit. Here it is both for his sake and for its sake, and the ברייתא still says it is unfit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from a ברייתא about the calf used for עגלה ערופה. It argues that a case with both purposes is treated as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עגלה ערופה must never have been made to work. If the calf was brought into the yoke only to nurse and it happened to thresh, it stays fit. If the owner meant it both to nurse (good for the calf) and to thresh (good for him), it is unfit. The גמרא reads this as a mixed case being treated like 'for his sake', so spreading the garment for both reasons should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a proof from a source
A team of cows yoked together
The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
For his benefit and for its benefit, the mixed case

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he brought it into the team of cows and it threshed –
phrases.notes: He meant only for the calf to nurse from its mother. The threshing just happened on its own.

phrases.english: it is fit.
If he did it so that it would nurse and thresh –
it is unfit.
But here it is for his sake and for its sake,
and it teaches that it is unfit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 6 knocked down the guest proof, the גמרא tries a fresh proof for the question from Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That doing something both for the object's good and for one's own benefit is treated as forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a calf put in the yoke to nurse and to thresh is unfit for עגלה ערופה.

steps.title: The calf is different because of a special verse
steps.stepSummary: The calf case proves nothing, because the פסוק disqualifies an עגלה ערופה after any work at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says 'that has not been worked with', meaning in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the calf proof. The עגלה ערופה has its own special rule from a פסוק, so it cannot teach us about the found garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'אשר לא עבד בה' is read as 'in any case'. Any work disqualifies the calf, even work mixed with something good for it. That strict rule belongs to עגלה ערופה only, so we cannot learn from it that a mixed case is forbidden with a found garment.

keyTerms.meaning: That has not been worked with
In any case, no matter how

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the verse says:
"that has not been worked with"
in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from עגלה ערופה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עגלה ערופה has a special verse that disqualifies it after any work, so it cannot be compared to the found garment.

steps.title: Then even the first case should be unfit
steps.stepSummary: If any work disqualifies the calf, then the first case, where it threshed by itself, should also be unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even the first case should also be unfit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If any work disqualifies the calf, why does the ברייתא say the calf that threshed by accident is fit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the verse disqualifies the calf after work 'in any case'. But the first case of the ברייתא has the calf threshing and still calls it fit. So 'in any case' cannot mean literally any work, and the rejection in Step 8 is now in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a challenge based on what was just said
The first clause of a source

steps.confusionAlert: This question attacks the answer in Step 8, not the original proof. The גמרא is checking whether 'in any case' can really be right, since the first case of the same ברייתא seems to contradict it.

phrases.english: If so,
then even the first case too should be unfit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection given in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 8 that the verse disqualifies the calf after any work at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first case of the same ברייתא has the calf threshing and still calls it fit. So 'any work at all' cannot be right as stated.

steps.title: The calf case is like the red heifer case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the calf case matches a משנה about the פרה אדומה. If a bird rested on it, it stays fit. If a male animal mounted it, it becomes unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only like that other case, as we learned in a משנה: if a bird rested on the heifer, it is fit. If a male animal mounted it, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 by pointing to a similar case about the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרה case, some things that happen to the animal on their own do not disqualify it, and others do: a male mounting it disqualifies even though the owner did nothing. The same is true of the calf: threshing that just happened while nursing does not disqualify it, but threshing the owner wanted does. Steps 12 and 13 explain where the line falls.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only comparable to this case
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: This is comparable only to this
as we learned:
phrases.notes: This משנה is about the פרה אדומה, the red heifer.

phrases.english: If a bird rested on it, it is fit
If a male mounted it, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לְהָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by comparing the calf to the פרה אדומה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any work at all disqualifies the calf, even threshing by itself
steps.terutzMaskana: Only certain kinds of work disqualify it, just as with the פרה

steps.title: Why the difference between the bird and the male?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the bird does not disqualify the heifer while the male does.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the difference in the פרה case. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases something happened to the animal without it doing real work on purpose. So we need a rule that tells the two cases apart.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the case brought in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What rule separates the bird (fit) from the male (unfit)?

steps.title: רב פפא: the two ways the word could have been written
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the two possible readings of the word in the פסוק. If it were only read as passive, even work done by itself would disqualify. If it were only read as active, only work the owner did would disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב פפא said: if the word were written עֻבַּד and read עֻבַּד, I would say even work done by itself disqualifies. If it were written עָבַד and read עָבַד, I would say it only disqualifies once he himself worked with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב פפא's teaching about the word in the פסוק of עגלה ערופה. Here he lays out what each reading alone would mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spelling (כתיב) and the way we read it aloud (קרי) are different here. The passive reading עֻבַּד means 'was worked', even with no person involved. The active reading עָבַד means 'he worked it', which requires the owner to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: How the word is written (its spelling)

phrases.english: In line with רב פפא
for רב פפא said:
phrases.notes: He is talking about the word in דברים 21:3, "אשר לא עֻבַּד בה".

phrases.english: If it were written "ubbad"
and we read it "ubbad"
I would say: even by itself.
And if it were written "avad" and we read it "avad"

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: עַד דַּעֲבַד בָּהּ אִיהוּ.
phrases.english: I would say: only once he himself worked with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reason comes from how the פסוק's word is written and read

steps.title: Only work the owner is pleased with disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The word is written עָבַד but read עֻבַּד, so עֻבַּד must be like עָבַד. Even work the animal does by itself disqualifies only when the owner is pleased with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that it is written עָבַד and read עֻבַּד, we need עֻבַּד to be like עָבַד. Just as עָבַד is work he is pleased with, so too עֻבַּד is work he is pleased with.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא combines the two readings into one rule: work disqualifies only if the owner is happy with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combining the readings means the work does not need to be done by the owner, but he must be pleased with it. This explains the פרה: the owner does not care about a bird, but he is glad the animal mated. It also answers step 9: when the calf threshed while nursing, the owner did not want the threshing, so it stays fit.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased with it, it suits him

steps.whatToRemember: Work that happens on its own disqualifies the עגלה ערופה or פרה אדומה only when the owner is pleased with it (נִיחָא לֵיהּ). That is why the calf that threshed by itself while nursing stays fit.
steps.confusionAlert: The owner does not have to do the work himself. He only has to be pleased with it, which is why the mating case disqualifies even though the animal did it on its own.

phrases.english: Now that it is written "avad"
and we read it "ubbad"
we need "ubbad" to be similar to "avad".
Just as "avad" is where he is pleased with it
so too "ubbad" is where he is pleased with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two readings from step 12 into the final rule
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only work the owner is pleased with (נִיחָא לֵיהּ) disqualifies, so the calf that threshed while nursing is fit

steps.title: How to use found wooden, copper and silver vessels and tools
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about found vessels and brings a ברייתא. The finder uses each kind of vessel in a way that helps it or at least does not damage it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: silver and copper vessels, he may use them, etc. The רבנן taught: one who finds wooden vessels uses them so they will not rot. Copper vessels he uses with hot water, but not on the fire, because that wears them down. Silver vessels he uses with cold water, but not hot, because that blackens them. Shovels and axes he uses on soft things, but not hard ones, because that damages them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section, quoting the next line of the משנה and bringing a ברייתא that gives the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea follows the earlier steps: the finder may use a lost object only in a way that is good for it, or at least does not harm it. For each material, the ברייתא allows the safe use and forbids the use that would damage it.

phrases.english: Silver vessels and copper vessels
he may use them, etc.
The rabbis taught:
One who finds wooden vessels uses them
so that they will not rot
copper vessels, he uses them with hot water
but not on the fire
because it wears them down.
silver vessels, he uses them with cold water
but not with hot water
because it blackens them.
Shovels and axes
he uses them on soft things
but not on hard things
because it damages them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלֵי כֶסֶף וּכְלֵי נְחוֹשֶׁת מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder may use found vessels only in ways that do not damage them

steps.title: Gold and glass vessels may not be touched
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that found gold and glass vessels may not be touched until אליהו comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Gold vessels and glass vessels, he may not touch them until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list with vessels the finder may not use at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike wood or copper, gold and glass are not harmed by sitting unused. Using them helps them in no way and only risks harm, so the finder must leave them alone. 'Until אליהו comes' means he keeps them for as long as it takes for the owner to be identified.

keyTerms.meaning: Until אליהו comes, meaning indefinitely, until the owner is identified

steps.whatToRemember: A finder may use a lost object only when the use is good for it, or at least safe for it. Objects that gain nothing from use, like gold and glass, may not be touched.

phrases.english: Gold vessels and glass vessels
he may not touch them
until אליהו comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלֵי זָהָב וּכְלֵי זְכוּכִית לֹא יִגַּע בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the case where no use is allowed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Found gold and glass vessels may not be used at all

steps.title: The same rules apply to a deposit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the rules for caring for a lost item also apply to a פקדון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same way the חכמים spoke about a lost item, they spoke about a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last steps continues. It says that the rules for how to care for a found item also apply to an item someone was given to watch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the ברייתא discussed a finder who uses and airs out found vessels so they don't spoil. Now it widens the rule to a שומר holding a פקדון. This addition sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit: an item given to someone to watch
In the same way that they said

phrases.english: In the manner that they said regarding a lost item
so they said regarding a deposit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּאֲבֵידָה כָּךְ אָמְרוּ בְּפִקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר cares for a פקדון the same way a finder cares for a lost item.

steps.title: Why is the watchman handling the deposit at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a watchman would need to care for a deposit, when the owner could take care of it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the deposit doing with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the watchman is the one using and caring for the item. The owner is around and can do it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a lost item, the owner isn't there, so the finder must take care of it. With a deposit, the owner can usually come and air out his own things. So the case in the ברייתא needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it doing with him? (why is he dealing with it?)

phrases.english: A deposit, what is it doing with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case described in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation would a שומר need to care for a פקדון himself?

steps.title: The owner went overseas
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר חמא, quoting רב ששת, answers that the owner of the deposit has gone overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר חמא said in the name of רב ששת: it is talking about a deposit whose owners went overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the owner traveled far away. Since he can't care for his item, the watchman must do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the deposit is just like a lost item: the owner is not available. That is why the same care rules apply. The question of step 17 is fully answered.

keyTerms.meaning: A country overseas, a faraway place

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Chama said that Rav Sheshet said:
It is about a deposit whose owners went
to a country overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is where the owner went overseas, so the שומר must care for the item.
steps.whatToRemember: A שומר only takes over caring for a פקדון when the owner is far away, which makes it like an אבידה.

steps.title: The משנה: an item beneath his dignity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if someone finds an item he would never normally carry, he does not have to take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found a sack or a basket, or anything he does not usually carry, he should not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. A person does not have to pick up a lost item that is beneath his dignity to carry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is a מצוה to return a lost item. Here the משנה gives an exception: a respected person who would never carry a sack in public does not have to. This quote sets up the גמרא's search for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: That it is not his way to carry

phrases.english: If he found a sack or a basket
[or any item] that it is not his way to take,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets.

phrases.english: he shall not take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One need not take a lost item that is beneath his dignity to carry.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn this rule from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה commands us to return lost items, an exception needs a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק allows a person to leave the item.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that one may leave a lost item that is beneath his dignity?

steps.title: Sometimes you may ignore a lost item
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word והתעלמת that there are times you may ignore a lost item and times you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "And you shall disregard": there are times you may disregard, and times you may not disregard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The word והתעלמת in the פסוק teaches that sometimes a person is allowed to ignore a lost item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says not to ignore a lost animal. But the ברייתא reads the extra word as hinting that ignoring is sometimes allowed. Which times are allowed is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall disregard / turn away
As the רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And you shall disregard"
there are times that you may disregard
and there are times that you may not disregard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word והתעלמת teaches that there are times one may ignore a lost item.

steps.title: The three cases where you may ignore it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists three cases: a כהן when the item is in a cemetery, an elder when it is beneath his dignity, and when his lost work time is worth more than the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he was a כהן and it is in the cemetery, or he was an elder and it is beneath his dignity, or his work was worth more than his fellow's item: for this it says "and disregard them."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains when a person may ignore a lost item. It gives three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is about a prohibition: a כהן may not become impure in a cemetery. The second is about honor, which is the משנה's case of an item beneath one's dignity. The third is about money: the finder would lose more from stopping work than the item is worth.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder, a respected older person

phrases.english: How so?
If he was a priest and it is in the cemetery,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה זָקֵן וְאֵינָהּ לְפִי כְּבוֹדוֹ,
phrases.english: or he was an elder and it is not fitting his dignity,
or his own work
was worth more than his fellow's item,
therefore it is said: "And disregard them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'times you may disregard' from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may ignore a lost item in three cases: a כהן and a cemetery, an elder for whom it is beneath his dignity, and when his work is worth more than the item.
steps.whatToRemember: Three exceptions to returning a lost item: איסור (a כהן in a cemetery), כבוד (an elder), and ממון (losing more money than the item is worth).

steps.title: Which case needed the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the three cases actually needed a פסוק to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what case was the verse needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which of the three cases really needed the פסוק. This sets up the next step, which goes through the options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a case could be known by logic alone, the פסוק is not needed for it. The גמרא wants to find the case the פסוק is really teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: For what was the verse needed?

phrases.english: For what case was the verse necessary?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the three cases listed in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three cases could not be known without the פסוק?

steps.title: The כהן case is obvious for two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the פסוק is for the כהן case. That is obvious, because an עשה cannot push aside a לא תעשה plus an עשה, and because we never push aside a prohibition for money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is for a כהן when the item is in a cemetery, that is obvious. Returning it is a positive commandment, while entering the cemetery breaks a prohibition and a positive commandment, and a positive commandment does not push aside a prohibition plus a positive commandment. Also, we do not push aside a prohibition for money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first case, the כהן in a cemetery, and says it doesn't need a פסוק. It gives two reasons why it is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: returning a lost item is only an עשה, while a כהן's impurity is a לא תעשה and an עשה together, and a weaker מצוה cannot push aside a stronger one. Reason two: a lost item is only money, and money never overrides an איסור. So the פסוק must be needed for a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment comes and pushes aside

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying a כהן must return the item. It is saying the opposite: of course he may leave it, and that is exactly why a פסוק is not needed for this case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses two big general rules found all over ש״ס: an עשה does not push aside a לא תעשה ועשה, and money never overrides an איסור.

phrases.english: If you say it is for a priest when it is in the cemetery,
that is obvious,
this is a positive commandment
phrases.notes: "This" is the מצוה to return a lost item, "you shall return them" (דברים 22:1).

phrases.english: and that is a prohibition and a positive commandment,
phrases.notes: "That" is a כהן becoming impure from the dead (ויקרא 21:1, 21:6).

phrases.english: and a positive commandment does not come and push aside
a prohibition together with a positive commandment,
And furthermore:
we do not push aside a prohibition for the sake of money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא לְכֹהֵן וְהִיא בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the כהן case as the reason the פסוק was needed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is already obvious from two general rules, so no פסוק is needed for it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that והתעלמת is needed for the כהן in a cemetery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עשה cannot override a לא תעשה ועשה, and money cannot override an איסור, so the case needs no פסוק.

steps.title: Maybe the verse teaches the case where his own loss is bigger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the word והתעלמת is needed for the case where a person's own loss is greater than the value of his friend's lost item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say the verse is needed for the case where his own loss is bigger than his friend's.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the כהן case, the גמרא tries a new answer: maybe the פסוק is teaching the third case from the ברייתא, where returning the item would cost him more than it is worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from step 23 is still open: which case actually needs a פסוק? The גמרא now points to the money case, where stopping work would cost him more than the item is worth. This is only a suggestion, and the גמרא will test it right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new suggestion after the last one was rejected
His own (here, his own loss of money or work time)
His friend, the other person (the owner of the lost item)

phrases.english: Rather, the verse is for when his own
is greater than that of his friend

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כהן case was rejected in step 24, the גמרא offers a different case as what the פסוק teaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three cases needs the word והתעלמת as its source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggests it is the case where his own loss is greater than his friend's.

steps.title: No, that rule comes from רב יהודה in the name of רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: the rule about one's own loss being greater already comes from a teaching of רב יהודה quoting רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is learned from what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. We don't need והתעלמת for the money case, because we already learn it from another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the תורה should teach something we couldn't learn otherwise. Since the money case already has its own source in רב יהודה's teaching, והתעלמת can't be for that case. So the search for what והתעלמת teaches goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out, it is learned (from a certain source)
An אמורא, a student of רב, who often reports his teacher's statements

phrases.english: That is learned from what רב יהודה said that רב said

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that והתעלמת is the source for the case where his own loss is greater. The rule itself stays true.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That rule already has a different source, so the פסוק of והתעלמת is not needed for it.

steps.title: רב יהודה's teaching begins with the פסוק 'אפס כי'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting רב יהודה's teaching in the name of רב, which starts from the פסוק 'אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: 'Only so that…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows the source it just mentioned. It begins quoting רב יהודה's teaching, which is built on a פסוק, and the quote continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line backs up the rejection in step 26 by bringing the actual source for the money case. Only the opening words of the פסוק appear here, so we have to wait to see how רב reads it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Only so that' — the opening words of the פסוק in דברים 15:4

phrases.english: As רב יהודה said that רב said
"Only so that
phrases.notes: דברים 15:4. The quote keeps going in the next lines of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source mentioned in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That the case of his own loss being greater already has a source outside of והתעלמת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב, reading the פסוק 'אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון' (דברים 15:4).
